node-1.label: A man in his 20s has a 6-year history of multiple growing papules superimposed on an asymptomatic firm plaque on the occipital scalp

node-2.label: At 3 years of age, scarlike macules appeared on the occipital scalp and coalesced to form a larger plaque with sparse hair; simultaneously, multiple brown-red, dome-shaped papules developed on the nose and gradually evolved to involve the cheeks

node-3.label: Rubbery plaques developed on the sacrococcygeal area, along with hypopigmented patches on the right buttock

node-4.label: The lesions were never ulcerated or inflamed, but hemorrhage occurred occasionally after rubbing

node-5.label: Physical examination revealed a group of unevenly distributed skin-colored-to-pink, discrete, coalescing papules superimposed on a firm plaque on the occipital scalp

node-6.label: The patient has no systemic symptoms or mental impairment and denied a family history of genetic disease

why.why: Scalp biopsy demonstrating dense dermal fibrosis with onionskin/whorled collagen bundles and perifollicular fibrosis (hamartomatous collagenoma) and facial papule histology of angiofibroma are classic TSC stigmata. Combined with sacral shagreen patch and hypopigmented macules, multiple major diagnostic criteria are fulfilled. Radiologist and pathologist analyses independently strongly support TSC; lack of genetic/imaging data leaves formal genetic confirmation incomplete but does not lower clinical probability. Confidence increased from 0.8 to 0.95.

Although scalp biopsy shows a hamartomatous collagenoma, histologic confirmation of facial angiofibroma plus sacral shagreen patch and hypopigmented macules demonstrates multifocal TSC stigmata. The radiologist explicitly states that the multifocal distribution excludes a localized hamartoma. Confidence reduced from 0.12 to 0.04.

Biopsy findings are benign hamartomatous collagenoma and angiofibroma with no malignant features; childhood onset, non-ulcerated course, and expert analyses confirm a benign process. Confidence reduced from 0.05 to 0.02.

Biopsy shows dermal fibrosis with perifollicular fibrosis but no significant inflammation, and the clinical course lacks inflammation or ulceration; multifocal TSC stigmata and expert analyses refute inflammatory scarring alopecia. Confidence reduced from 0.03 to 0.01.

node-11.label: Scalp biopsy shows dense dermal fibrosis with whorled/onionskin collagen bundles, perifollicular fibrosis, decreased follicles, and capillary ectasia (hamartomatous collagenoma)

node-12.label: Facial papule histology is consistent with angiofibroma
